answer: Each agent claims a unique cell on a capacity-bounded stake trellis whose row limits are fixed by a basalt hardness parameter that cannot be raised without burning capital. New identities are admitted only after a yarrow-style sequential selection of distinct recent work digests; any two clones that share a parent hash collide and forfeit the entire row deposit. Because influence is strictly 1/n per occupied cell, a farm of k aliases locks k times the stake yet gains only linear weight while honest single-cell agents keep full power.
